description: Close the persistence gap so creating, editing, and renaming templates actually save to disk via TemplateService. Today TemplateEditorWindow.SaveButton_Click only mutates an in-memory SlideTemplate and never calls the service, and TemplateManagerPanel's New/Rename paths never persist (Rename just raises an unconsumed EditTemplateRequested event). Make the editor persist on Save (CreateAsync for new, UpdateAsync for existing) and wire the manager's New and Edit(Rename) buttons to the persisting editor. Depends on FEAT-001 (the service must be injected and the panel reachable). SlideTemplate.Id defaults to a fresh Guid, so use an explicit IsNewTemplate flag — not empty-Id — to pick create vs update.
steps: In WorshipPlayer.Presenter\Views\Templates\TemplateEditorWindow.xaml.cs, add 'public bool IsNewTemplate { get; set; }'.

Change SaveButton_Click to 'async void'. After the existing code that copies control values into _template, guard 'if (_templateService == null) { WasSaved = false; DialogResult = false; Close(); return; }'. Then in a try/catch: if IsNewTemplate, set '_template.Id = string.Empty;' then 'await _templateService.CreateAsync(_template);' else 'await _templateService.UpdateAsync(_template);'. Only on success set 'WasSaved = true; DialogResult = true; Close();'. On exception show a MessageBox ('Failed to save template: ' + ex.Message) and leave the window open (do not set DialogResult).

In WorshipPlayer.Presenter\Views\Templates\TemplateManagerPanel.xaml.cs NewButton_Click, set 'editor.IsNewTemplate = true;' before editor.ShowDialog(). (Editor Template stays a fresh SlideTemplate for the new case.)

Rewrite RenameButton_Click as 'async void' to open the editor on the selected custom template: return if selected is null or selected.IsBuiltIn or _templateService == null; fetch 'var full = await _templateService.GetByIdAsync(selected.Id);' return if null; create 'var editor = new TemplateEditorWindow { IsNewTemplate = false, TemplateService = _templateService, Owner = Window.GetWindow(this) };' then 'editor.Template = full;' (set Template AFTER TemplateService so the editor has the service when saving); 'editor.ShowDialog();' then 'if (editor.WasSaved) await RefreshTemplatesAsync();'. This also satisfies the previously-unconsumed EditTemplateRequested intent, so the event may be left as-is or removed if unused.

Optional UX: in WorshipPlayer.Presenter\Views\Templates\TemplateManagerPanel.xaml relabel the RenameButton Content from 'Rename' to 'Edit' for clarity (it now opens the full editor). Keep the x:Name and Click handler unchanged.
Build the solution and run the template tests.
acceptance_criteria: The build command completes with 0 errors (pre-existing warnings allowed).
TemplateEditorWindow persists via ITemplateService.CreateAsync when IsNewTemplate is true and via UpdateAsync otherwise, and only closes with DialogResult true after a successful save.

TemplateManagerPanel New opens the editor with IsNewTemplate=true; the Edit/Rename button opens the editor loaded with the selected custom template's full SlideTemplate and refreshes the list after a save.

A newly created or edited custom template is written to the <AppBase>\Templates folder (via the service) and reappears when the list is refreshed; built-in templates remain non-editable/non-deletable as enforced by the service.
Duplicate and Delete continue to work; running TemplateServiceTests still passes all 20 tests.
findings:
Persistence gap closed.

1. TemplateEditorWindow.xaml.cs: added 'public bool IsNewTemplate { get; set; }' (next to WasSaved). SaveButton_Click is now 'async void'. After copying control values into _template it guards: if (_templateService == null) { WasSaved=false; DialogResult=false; Close(); return; }. Then try/catch: when IsNewTemplate it sets _template.Id = string.Empty and awaits CreateAsync(_template); otherwise awaits UpdateAsync(_template). Only on success sets WasSaved=true, DialogResult=true, Close(). On exception shows MessageBox('Failed to save template: ' + ex.Message) and leaves the window open (DialogResult untouched). 'Exception' resolves via ImplicitUsings (enabled in WorshipPlayer.Presenter.csproj).

2. TemplateManagerPanel.xaml.cs NewButton_Click: editor now created with IsNewTemplate = true (Template stays a fresh SlideTemplate for the new case).

3. TemplateManagerPanel.xaml.cs RenameButton_Click: rewritten to 'async void'. Returns if selection null / selected.IsBuiltIn / _templateService == null. Fetches full = await GetByIdAsync(selected.Id); returns if null. Creates editor { IsNewTemplate=false, TemplateService=_templateService, Owner=Window.GetWindow(this) }, sets editor.Template = full AFTER TemplateService (so the service is present at save time), ShowDialog(), then 'if (editor.WasSaved) await RefreshTemplatesAsync();'. The now-unused EditTemplateRequested event was left in place (harmless CS0067 warning only).

4. TemplateManagerPanel.xaml: RenameButton Content relabeled 'Rename' -> 'Edit' (x:Name and Click handler unchanged).

Verification: dotnet build = 0 errors (6 warnings, all pre-existing/benign: the documented MediaLibraryPanel._currentView CS0414, ChordChartWindow CS8604, WaveformEditorWindow._inReviewMode CS0414, plus TemplateManagerPanel.EditTemplateRequested CS0067 which is expected now that Rename opens the editor directly). dotnet test TemplateServiceTests = 20/20 passed.
